r: **Six freedoms** to citizens – **seven originally**; the 7th, property, was deleted
**Articles 19–22** (four Articles); Arts. 14–16 belong to the Equality group
**Form associations or unions** or **co-operative societies** (co-operatives added by the **97th, 2011**)
**Move freely throughout the territory of India**
**Reside and settle** in any part of India
Acquire, hold and dispose of **property** – deleted by the **44th Amendment, 1978**
**Practise any profession**, or carry on any **occupation, trade or business**
Deleted 1978; now Art. 300A, a legal right (**44th Amendment Act, 1978**)
New right to **form co-operative societies** in 19(1)(c); also **Article 43B** and **Part IXB**
**26 January 1950** – Art. 19 of the original Constitution provided freedom of expression
Protection in respect of conviction for offences
Protection of life and personal liberty
Arrest and detention; preventive detention without an **Advisory Board**: max **three months**
**The most essential ingredient of democracy** among the freedoms
**Freedom of the press is not named in the Constitution**; it is **implied in / secured under 19(1)(a)**
Speech is protected **irrespective of the medium of communication** – press, TV, internet
The **right to know, receive and impart information** is part of 19(1)(a); RTI itself is not named in the Constitution
**May be pre-censored**, unlike the press, because they **reach larger audiences**
**Hoisting the National Flag** (also on private buildings) – **19(1)(a)**
**Naveen Jindal (2004)** – industrialist Naveen Jindal's PIL in the Delhi HC; the Flag Code is only executive instructions
**Right to silence** (not singing the National Anthem)
**Bijoe Emmanuel v. Kerala (1986)** – speech and conscience (Art. 25)
**State of UP v. Raj Narain (1975)**; voters' right to know candidates
Telecast; no government monopoly on airwaves

1.x: **National Anthem:** compelling anyone to sing it violates speech/expression and conscience, and **no law obliges anyone to sing it** (the 1971 Act punishes only preventing its singing).
**Internet access** is linked to **Article 19** (Anuradha Bhasin); privacy and shelter are Art. 21 rights.

2.x: In a democracy the right to freedom = **freedom with reasonable restrictions**.

r: Eight: **sovereignty and integrity**, **security of State**, **friendly relations with foreign States**, **public order**, **decency or morality**, **contempt of court**, **defamation**, **incitement to an offence**
Sovereignty and integrity; **public order** (not morality, not security of State)
General public interest; **professional/technical qualifications**; **State trade or monopoly**
**Sedition**, **views opposing the Government**, **unbecoming criticism**, "general public interest", economic grounds
**Slander = spoken** (oral), libel = written; civil (tort) and criminal liability
**Public order, friendly relations, incitement**; rewrote 19(6) – qualifications and State monopoly
Nature of the right, purpose, extent and urgency of the evil, proportionality
**Courts**; a restriction must **not eclipse the right**, must safeguard the **interest of the general public** and weigh **prevailing social values and needs**
**Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar (1962)**
Landmark judgment on **sedition**: s.124A IPC valid only for incitement to violence or public disorder
For **citizens only** – not foreigners, not a company as a legal person (citizen shareholders may sue)
Guaranteed **only to citizens**; life and liberty, equality before law and freedom of religion extend to foreigners too
Cannot claim **freedom of trade and profession** (19(1)(g))
**State action**; **Kaushal Kishor (2023)**: Arts. 19 and 21 enforceable against **non-State actors** too

A person whose movement is taken away by **imprisonment or detention** keeps his **freedom of expression** – he may write and publish books (State of Maharashtra v. Prabhakar Pandurang Sanzgiri, 1966)
Only for an emergency on **war or external aggression** (44th Amendment), not armed rebellion
Suspends only the enforcement of the rights named

4.x: The Article suspended when an emergency is imposed = **Article 19**.

r: Must be **peaceful and unarmed**; excludes violent or **armed** gatherings
SC: peaceful protest is everybody's right but **must not disturb other citizens** or occupy public space
Not an FR – **only a legal right**
Centre defends the curbs (25 Jun 2026); **INSAF (2020)** – only associations in **active politics** may be barred from foreign funds
Entry and settlement of outsiders may be limited to protect **Scheduled Tribes** (Inner Line areas)
State may prescribe **professional or technical qualifications** and run a trade **to the exclusion of citizens** (State monopoly) – inserted by the **1st Amendment**
**No right to a dangerous or immoral trade** (e.g. trafficking)
Ban on the journal **Cross Roads** struck down; "public order" then not a ground → 1st Amendment
Sedition valid only for **incitement to violence**
**Newsprint policy fixing pages** violated press freedom
**Sec. 66A IT Act** struck down – vague, overbroad
Internet shutdowns must be **proportionate, temporary, published**

7.x: **BNS, 2023** replaced the IPC; **BNSS, 2023** replaced the CrPC (statutory **Zero FIR**, video recording of search and seizure).
